body: Hi I made a pull request as the easiest way to show what the changes are https://github.com/godotengine/godot-headers/pull/112

Looks like the change to `Material` (possibly #76023) needing resyncing these headers.

I've actually no idea how this is done so will try and look into how to keep these up to date, it's possible some changes in 3.7 will also require an update here.

I've gone through the instructions in `godot-headers`, and generated new headers for the current 3.6 branch.
I don't get any diffs required as in your PR, only the small addition of an `_invalidate_fonts` function (which looks internal and may well not be required).

The lines:
```
				"name": "material",
				"type": "SpatialMaterial,ORMSpatialMaterial,ShaderMaterial",
```
Look correct.

`SpatialMaterial`, `ORMSpatialMaterial` and `ShaderMaterial` are all now derived from `Material3D`, which in turn is derived from `Material`.

`ArrayMesh` is derived from `Mesh`, not the other way around. `Mesh` is derived from `Resource`.

I'm not clear on what you are trying to do and what is going wrong, whether it is a problem within Godot ecosystem or external.

This may need some contributors more familiar with GDNative to help guide you (I've never used it, aside from basic testing).

I'll be honest I don't understand all intricacies of the code I'm working with - I didn't write it, I'm just trying to make it work.

I've been getting the haskell bindings working (I've forked them at https://github.com/JonnyRa/godot-haskell as they were largely unmaintained) and upgraded them to use godot 3.6.2. (The originals are at https://github.com/SimulaVR/godot-haskell but the master branch hasn't been touched for 5 years and doesn't compile).  Thankfully upgrading through godot versions is documented and part of the process is pulling a git submodule which points at the godot_headers repo and then running some code generation which uses the api.json document to generate a load of haskell code

My understanding of the api.json document is it is supposed to basically be a machine readable version of the c api - effectively a schema and that it should broadly match what is in the documentation as well.

The issue is that the api.json contains things that don't really make a lot of sense.  So the generated haskell code then won't compile as some of the functions are trying to pass types that don't match.  The Haskell compiler is quite strict about these things (which is one of it's main good points as well as main pain points as a language 😆 ).  As part of the upgrade of the haskell bindings I've been updating the api.json where the haskell codegenerator and compiler have found inconsistencies - eg rather than fiddle with the generated code I've been fixing the schema instead - that allows me to rerun the code gen without overwriting a load of manual changes.

The examples saying that a property can be one of 3 types is odd - you could express that in Haskell in various ways but (whilst I'm definitely not a c or Gdscript expert) I didn't know you could express that sort of thing in those languages - the OO way of having multiple different types that can be passed into a single function is generally to have a common base class. 

To look at a specific example of one of those ones that has 3 types (I picked the change at line 40842), one of the places where there are 3 types given is on CanvasItem with the property called "material" (you can add more context to the diff by clicking the little up arrow buttons on github in the line number column - that let's you see what types the properties live on).  If you check the docs it says that the function accepts an object of type Material (https://docs.godotengine.org/en/3.6/classes/class_canvasitem.html#class-canvasitem-property-material) which corresponds with the change I've made.

In the case of the ArrayMesh one it is about the property called "mesh" on GLTFMesh, where again the Haskell compiler and the docs seem to agree - it is supposed to be an ArrayMesh https://docs.godotengine.org/en/3.6/classes/class_gltfmesh.html#class-gltfmesh-property-mesh.

Is api.json generated somehow rather than just a maintained schema?  If that's the case it seems like there may be a bug with the generation in some of these cases... obviously that's trickier to fix than just a manually maintained schema but an understandable thing to do given the size of the document.  Since it's clearly correct most of the time it might be easiest to just maintain a small number of fixes to the generated output - about 15 mistakes in 200k+ lines isn't bad!  Obviously not my call to make though.

Hopefully that makes sense

Cheers

Jonny

> I'll be honest I don't understand all intricacies of the code I'm working with - I didn't write it, I'm just trying to make it work.

> but the master branch hasn't been touched for 5 years and doesn't compile

5 years is a long time and the engine has changed a lot since 5 years ago.

Yeah I was a little worried about it but it's fixed now and it wasn't too painful.  Took a couple of weeks.  I've only gone up to the 3.6.2 LTS version (it was on 3.1) though I'm sure converting to GDExtension would be more involved.

Even though it's got a bit old the haskell project seems to have been well thought through and there was enough documentation there to do the upgrade 😌
